Estimate DNS Parameters from Factors using YUIMA

Source: R/dns-simulation.r
estimate_dns_parameters_yuima.Rd

Estimates DNS model parameters from factor time series using YUIMA's advanced estimation methods.

Usage

estimate_dns_parameters_yuima(
  factor_data,
  initial_params = NULL,
  estimation_method = "qmle",
  delta_t = 1/252
)

Arguments

factor_data

Data frame or matrix. Time series of DNS factors (level, slope, curvature). Columns named beta1, beta2 and beta3 are used when present, so a parameters frame from fit_dns_model can be passed directly; otherwise the first three numeric columns are taken, after any Date column is dropped.

initial_params

List. Initial parameter values for optimization.

estimation_method

Character. Method for parameter estimation ("qmle" or "gmm").

delta_t

Numeric. Time step between observations in years.

Value

A list containing:

  • estimated_params: Estimated model parameters

  • yuima_model: The fitted YUIMA model

  • fit_result: Full result from the YUIMA estimation

Details

This function uses the YUIMA package's estimation capabilities to fit an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process to observed factor time series. It provides more rigorous statistical estimation than standard regression methods.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Assuming factor_data is a data frame with columns: Date, beta1, beta2, beta3
factors <- factor_data[, c("beta1", "beta2", "beta3")]
initial <- list(
  kappa = c(0.02, 0.3, 0.5),
  theta = c(0.04, -0.02, 0.01),
  sigma = c(0.005, 0.01, 0.02)
)
est_result <- estimate_dns_parameters_yuima(factors, initial)
} # }
